continuationFrom.result: Quorum-staged sender state survived bounded enumeration and a one-host three-process etcd confirmation, while neither RESEND nor WITHHOLD guaranteed exactly-once recipient delivery under indistinguishable response-loss worlds.

factsFixedFromPrimarySources.fact: HTTP defines a method as idempotent when multiple identical requests have the same intended server effect as one request; the definition does not prohibit separate logging or other non-idempotent side effects for each request.

SQLite atomic commit makes all changes within one transaction appear to occur together or not at all, including interruption by a process or operating-system crash, subject to the documented storage assumptions.
SQLite documents serializable ACID transactions and tests interrupted transactions with a dedicated crash and power-failure harness.
Reliable messages require stable identifiers and acknowledgements, while crashes can separate message processing from acknowledgement observation.

researchQuestion: Under which minimal ordering and atomicity assumptions can a receiver turn retries after an unknown response into exactly one durable modeled effect, and where does that claim stop when the real effect leaves the receiver database?

model.kind: finite receiver state machine with one delivery ID, one accepted digest, one conflicting digest, two clients, persistent marker and effect fields, and one crash that clears only an in-flight step

protocols.claim: Apply the durable effect first, then write the deduplication marker.
protocols.expectedFailure: A crash after the effect but before the marker lets a retry apply the effect again.

protocols.claim: Write the deduplication marker first, then apply the durable effect.
protocols.expectedFailure: A crash after the marker but before the effect makes a retry return replay even though no effect exists.

protocols.claim: Write the delivery marker and modeled effect record in one atomic receiver transaction.
protocols.expectedBoundary: Can qualify only when the entire adjudicated effect shares that transaction; external physical or remote effects remain outside the claim.

model.exploration: Full breadth-first enumeration to a fixed point with deterministic transition order; no random sampling or depth cutoff.

invariants.R1_AT_MOST_ONE_EFFECT: The durable effect count never exceeds one.
invariants.R2_MARKER_EFFECT_ATOMIC: The marker and modeled effect are both absent or both present with the same digest.
invariants.R3_REPLAY_IMPLIES_EFFECT: A replay response is reachable only when exactly one effect exists.
invariants.R4_CONFLICT_NEVER_MUTATES: A conflicting digest never replaces the accepted marker or effect digest.
invariants.R5_ONE_SUCCESSFUL_DELIVERY: Once both clients terminate, exactly one modeled effect exists.

model.successRule: ATOMIC_INBOX_EFFECT alone must pass R1-R5; the other two protocols must retain their shortest discovered crash counterexamples. JavaScript and independently written Python enumerators must agree on graph sizes and minimal counterexample lengths.

topology.receiver: one separately spawned Python HTTP process at a time
topology.receiverStorage: three fresh SQLite files, rollback journal mode, synchronous FULL
topology.modeledEffect: one row in the SQLite effects table, atomically committed with one deliveries row

fixedCases.schedule: Insert delivery and effect inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, terminate the receiver with exit 86 before COMMIT, restart on the same database, retry twice, then submit a conflicting digest.
Commit delivery and effect, terminate the receiver with exit 87 before the HTTP response, restart on the same database, retry twice, then submit a conflicting digest.
Issue one hundred concurrent identical PUT requests from Node, then submit one invalid delivery ID and one invalid digest.

criteria.C1: After the before-commit crash, the first retry returns 201 created, the second returns 200 replay, and exactly one effect exists.
criteria.C2: After the after-commit crash, both retries return 200 replay and exactly one effect exists.
criteria.C3: Both accepted delivery IDs reject a different outcome digest with 409 and preserve the original digest.
criteria.C4: Among one hundred concurrent identical requests, exactly one returns 201 and ninety-nine return 200, with one delivery row and one effect row.
criteria.C5: Malformed delivery IDs and digests return 400 and create no additional effect.
criteria.C6: An independent Node auditor opens every committed SQLite database read-only, passes PRAGMA integrity_check, reconstructs row cardinality and crash outcomes from persisted artifacts, and verifies every synthetic acknowledgement HMAC.

confirmation.stopRule: Any failed C1-C6 criterion, database integrity failure, second effect row, accepted conflicting digest, or changed frozen script hash makes the confirmation non-qualifying.

claimBoundary.maySupport: Exactly one SQLite-modeled effect under the three fixed one-host crash, retry, conflict, malformed-input, and concurrency cases.
mayNotSupport: exactly-once physical actuation, payment, email, or a remote service call
a side effect not transactionally co-located with the receiver marker
multiple physical hosts or independent storage failure domains
a real network partition, reordering, duplication proxy, or permanent outage
host or disk loss, Byzantine behavior, production authentication, or production keys
an unbounded proof of exactly-once delivery

nextRungIfQualified: Replace the SQLite effect row with a durable outbox and a separately hosted idempotent sink; inject message and acknowledgement loss independently, then move sender consensus, receiver inbox, and the sink onto distinct physical hosts.
